scope: Global datasets referenced by pff_4.js and modules/timeSeriesAnthro.js. Custom-prepared assets (e.g. simplified GAUL, OSM rasters, GRIP rasterised AADT) are listed under their parent global source. Thresholds + masks shown are the in-script defaults; user UI overrides them at runtime.
intended_uses: Run-metadata sidecar (the export-settings JSON should embed only entries with status=active and resolved active_in_run=true)
Per-section information (i) buttons in the GEE app and QGIS plugin (key = id; tooltip body = description + citation.text + documentation)
Workshop / docs page enumerating sources (group + role_in_pff + citation)
Forward-looking inventory: status=queued entries are NOT used by pff_4 today but are referenced in code or docs and would be ready to wire up

status_definitions.active: Used in every default run of pff_4.js (or always-on in modules consumed by it).
status_definitions.optional_default_off: Code path exists and is reachable but the include flag / UI default is OFF. Becomes active only if a user (or a script change) flips the flag.
status_definitions.queued: Referenced in commented-out code, docs notes, or older module variants — not loaded in the current run path. Listed so the workshop can discuss them and so swap-in is straightforward.
status_definitions.deprecated: Was used in a previous version; superseded by another entry. Retained for provenance only.

groups.forest_cover: Tree-cover / forest-extent sources used to build the Tier-0 forest baseline
groups.forest_reference: Reference layers shown for visual comparison only (not used in the analysis chain)
groups.administrative: Country / sub-national boundaries and AOI definition
groups.protected_areas: Legal protection used in the slope/protected-area rescue tier
groups.terrain: DEM / slope used in the steep-terrain rescue tier
groups.built_up: Built-up settlement extent (small / large) for the disturbance buffers
groups.population: Population grids (currently used only via GHSL-POP masking; LandScan loaded but unused in the analysis chain)
groups.land_cover_agriculture: Cropland and pasture sources for the agriculture exclusion
groups.roads_infrastructure: Roads used for the road-buffer disturbance distance
groups.disturbance_history: Forest-loss / deforestation-year layers used in the disturbance composite
groups.water_waterways: Navigable rivers / canals (currently loaded but not in default disturbance composite)
groups.ancillary_unused: Datasets only referenced in commented-out alternatives

datasets.name: Hansen Global Forest Change
datasets.role_in_pff: Primary tree-cover source for the 'Hansen GFC' and 'Agreement / Combined' modes; supplies treecover2000 (canopy %) and lossyear (annual loss). Also feeds the disturbance composite (Hansen loss before analysisYear) used by forest_disturbances().
datasets.description: Global maps of 21st-century forest cover change at 30 m, derived from Landsat time series. The product reports tree-canopy density in 2000 (treecover2000, 0–100%) and the year of forest loss (lossyear, 0–24 → 2001–2024) per pixel. PFF treats canopy density as a continuous treecover input and uses lossyear to subtract pixels lost up to the analysis year.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: tree2000.gt(threshold) AND (no loss OR loss after analysisYear); selfMask. Threshold defaults to 10% canopy in the UI, user-adjustable 0–100%.

citation.text: Hansen, M.C., Potapov, P.V., Moore, R., Hancher, M., Turubanova, S.A., Tyukavina, A., Thau, D., Stehman, S.V., Goetz, S.J., Loveland, T.R., Kommareddy, A., Egorov, A., Chini, L., Justice, C.O., Townshend, J.R.G. (2013). High-Resolution Global Maps of 21st-Century Forest Cover Change. Science 342, 850–853.

datasets.name: GLAD Global Land Cover and Land Use 2000–2020 (v2)
datasets.version: v2 (Potapov et al. 2022, updated 2023 to add 2005/2010/2015 + revised built-up)
datasets.role_in_pff: Primary tree-cover source for the 'GLAD LULC' (default) and 'Agreement / Combined' modes; encodes tree height (m) per pixel which PFF thresholds to a binary forest mask. Also exported as raw tree-height layer 02a so users can re-threshold in QGIS.
datasets.description: First fully consistent 30 m global LCLU + change product derived from the Landsat archive. Tree height was modelled with a regression tree calibrated against GEDI lidar canopy structure measurements; classes 25–48 (and 125–148 over wetlands) encode tree height in metres up to 26 m. PFF remaps these classes back to height-in-metres and thresholds (default ≥ 5 m) to define forest. The OceanMask layer (≤1 = land) excludes ocean pixels.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Image for analysisYear masked to land via OceanMask ≤ 1; classes 25–48 / 125–148 remapped to integer heights 3–26 m; height ≥ user threshold (default 5 m) gives binary forest. For raw export the height image is unmasked to 0 and cast to Byte.

citation.text: Potapov, P., Hansen, M.C., Pickens, A., Hernandez-Serna, A., Tyukavina, A., Turubanova, S., Zalles, V., Li, X., Khan, A., Stolle, F., Harris, N., Song, X.-P., Baggett, A., Kommareddy, I., Kommareddy, A. (2022). The Global 2000–2020 Land Cover and Land Use Change Dataset Derived From the Landsat Archive: First Results. Frontiers in Remote Sensing 3, 856903.

datasets.name: Forest Landscape Integrity Index (FLII)
datasets.role_in_pff: Reference layer only — discretised into low (≤6.0) / medium (>6.0 & <9.6) / high (≥9.6) integrity bins and shown in the legend group 'Reference: FLII (high/med)' for visual comparison with PFF Primary Forest output.
datasets.description: A continuous 0–10 score per ~300 m forest pixel quantifying anthropogenic modification of forest landscapes, integrating observed pressures (infrastructure, agriculture), inferred pressures (deforestation, edge effects) and loss of forest connectivity. Higher = more intact.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: expression remap to 3-class (0/2/3); masked to country + buffer; selfMask.

citation.text: Grantham, H.S., Duncan, A., Evans, T.D., Jones, K.R., Beyer, H.L., Schuster, R., Walston, J., Ray, J.C., Robinson, J.G., Callow, M., Clements, T., Costa, H.M., DeGemmis, A., Elsen, P.R., Ervin, J., Franco, P., Goldman, E., Goetz, S., Hansen, A., Hofsvang, E., Jantz, P., Jupiter, S., Kang, A., Langhammer, P., Laurance, W.F., Lieberman, S., Linkie, M., Malhi, Y., Maxwell, S., Mendez, M., Mittermeier, R., Murray, N.J., Possingham, H., Radachowsky, J., Saatchi, S., Samper, C., Silverman, J., Shapiro, A., Strassburg, B., Stevens, T., Stokes, E., Taylor, R., Tear, T., Tizard, R., Venter, O., Visconti, P., Wang, S., Watson, J.E.M. (2020). Anthropogenic modification of forests means only 40% of remaining forests have high ecosystem integrity. Nature Communications 11, 5978.

datasets.name: Forest Data Partnership — Forest Persistence v0
datasets.role_in_pff: Reference layer only — thresholded at 0.90 and shown as 'Reference: Forest Persistence (FDaP)' for visual comparison with PFF Primary Forest output.
datasets.description: Per-pixel score (0–1) indicating the presence of undisturbed forest in 2020 at 30 m. Built via a convergence-of-evidence approach combining multiple disturbance and forest-management datasets. Coverage is ±80° latitude; some regions (China, Russia, Australia, NZ) lack regionally specific inputs in the ensemble.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: .gt(0.90) for the reference visualisation; otherwise unmodified.

citation.text: Forest Data Partnership / Google (2024). Forest Persistence v0 (2020). Community data product, not yet peer-reviewed.

datasets.license: CC-BY 4.0; required attribution: 'This dataset is produced by Google for the Forest Data Partnership.'

datasets.name: FAO GAUL 2024 — Level 0 (countries)
datasets.role_in_pff: Defines the country list, the AOI polygon for country-bounded analysis, and (via the simplified + raster derivatives) provides fast country masking for distance transforms and tile-level updateMask().

derived_assets.preprocessing: Simplified to 0.001° tolerance and diced to ≤10k vertices per polygon; used for IDN, THA, DZA, AUS, CHN where original GAUL polygons exceed GEE's vertex limit on .geometry().
Rasterised at 500 m with country code (gaul0_code) per pixel; used for fast updateMask country clipping (avoids a per-tile vector .clip()).

datasets.description: Vector dataset of country and sub-national administrative units harmonised by FAO from UN-SALB and partner sources, with country boundaries reconciled against the official UN-Map 2018. PFF uses Level 0 only (country boundaries).
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Filter by gaul0_name; for vertex-overflow countries swap in the simplified FC. For raster operations use the 500 m raster equality mask.

citation.text: FAO (2024). Global Administrative Unit Layers (GAUL) 2024. FAO, Rome.

datasets.name: World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA)
datasets.role_in_pff: Drives the protected-area rescue tier (Tier 1.3): forest pixels that fall inside legally protected areas of selected IUCN categories AND were established at least N years before the analysis year are kept even if they would otherwise be excluded by disturbance buffers. UI default IUCN selection = strict (Ia, Ib, II); years_protected = 30.
datasets.description: Most up-to-date global database of protected areas, updated monthly, managed by UNEP-WCMC with IUCN/WCPA. Each polygon carries IUCN_CAT, STATUS, STATUS_YR (year designated), and DESIG_ENG.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Pre-filter: STATUS ≠ 'Proposed', STATUS ≠ 'Not Reported', DESIG_ENG ≠ 'UNESCO-MAB Biosphere Reserve'. Reduce to image by min(STATUS_YR) for the year filter. Per-IUCN-category masks built once at startup and cached. At analysis time, OR together the user-selected categories' masks.

citation.text: UNEP-WCMC and IUCN (2026). Protected Planet: The World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA). UNEP-WCMC and IUCN, Cambridge, UK.

datasets.license: Standard WDPA terms — non-commercial use allowed; cite UNEP-WCMC + IUCN with download month/year

datasets.name: JAXA ALOS World 3D-30m DSM
datasets.role_in_pff: Source DEM for the steep-slope rescue tier (Tier 1.2): forest pixels on steep slopes are kept even if inside disturbance buffers. Also exported (03b) as DEM and slope sidecars for QGIS users to re-derive themselves.
datasets.description: Global 30 m DSM compiled from ALOS PRISM tri-stereo imagery (2006–2011), updated with other open-access DSMs in v3 to fill voids and improve quality. PFF takes the DSM band, mosaics, and computes slope on the fly.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: select('DSM').mosaic(); slope via ee.Terrain.slope after setDefaultProjection EPSG:4326 @ 30 m; .gt(slopeToKeepValue) for the rescue mask.

citation.text: Tadono, T., Nagai, H., Ishida, H., Oda, F., Naito, S., Minakawa, K., Iwamoto, H. (2016). Generation of the 30 m-mesh Global Digital Surface Model by ALOS PRISM. ISPRS Archives XLI-B4, 157–162. (Note: JAXA's own reference list titles this 'Initial Validation of the 30 m-mesh…' — the published title at the DOI is 'Generation of…'.) See also Takaku et al. (2020) for v3 updates.

datasets.license: Free for research use with attribution to JAXA

datasets.name: JRC GHSL — Settlement Model (SMOD) P2023A v2.0
datasets.role_in_pff: Provides the 'built-up small' (rural cluster) and 'built-up large' (urban centre) settlement masks used by the disturbance buffers. Default ON (includeGHSL=true). Combined with WSF EVO via OR for the small bucket.
datasets.description: Degree-of-Urbanisation classification produced by joint inference over GHS-POP (population grid) and GHS-BUILT-S (built-up surface). Codes 11–12 = rural / village clusters; >12 = urban-centre / dense-urban. The accompanying GHS-POP grid provides the population mask used to drop unpopulated SMOD pixels.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Per target year, ghslLowDensity = SMOD ∈ [11,12]; ghslHighDensity = SMOD > 12. Masked by GHS_POP > 0 (drops uninhabited SMOD pixels). Output: 1 = built-up small, 2 = built-up large.

citation.text: Pesaresi, M., Schiavina, M., Politis, P., Freire, S., Krasnodebska, K., Uhl, J.H., Carioli, A., Corbane, C., Dijkstra, L., Florio, P., Freire, S., Maffenini, L., Tommasi, P. (2024). Advances on the Global Human Settlement Layer by Joint Assessment of Earth Observation and Population Survey Data. International Journal of Digital Earth 17(1).

datasets.name: DLR World Settlement Footprint Evolution
datasets.role_in_pff: Supplements GHSL SMOD for the built-up-small bucket: WSF EVO captures small/rural settlements that GHSL at 1 km can miss. Default ON (includeWSF=true).
datasets.description: Annual 30 m global settlement extent from 1985 to 2015 derived from Landsat-5/-7 time series anchored on WSF2015. Each pixel value is the year of first settlement detection; pixels that were never settled are excluded.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: wsfEvo.mosaic().lte(year) → binary settlement-by-year mask; combined into builtUpSmall via OR.

citation.text: Marconcini, M., Metz-Marconcini, A., Üreyen, S., Palacios-Lopez, D., Hanke, W., Bachofer, F., Zeidler, J., Esch, T., Gorelick, N., Kakarla, A., Paganini, M., Strano, E. (2020). Outlining where humans live, the World Settlement Footprint 2015. Scientific Data 7, 242.

datasets.name: GISD30 — Global 30 m Impervious Surface Dynamic 1985–2020
datasets.role_in_pff: Optional supplementary built-up source. Currently DISABLED by default (includeGISD=false) due to rock-formation false positives. Listed in code as a flag-flippable input for the small built-up bucket.
datasets.description: Global 30 m impervious-surface dynamic dataset from time-series Landsat on GEE. Pixel value encodes year of impervious onset. Validated to 90.1% overall accuracy, κ = 0.865 against 23,322 global samples.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: gisd30.lte(year-1985) for binary impervious-by-year mask; selfMask. Would OR into builtUpSmall if includeGISD were flipped on.

citation.text: Zhang, X., Liu, L., Zhao, T., Gao, Y., Chen, X., Mi, J. (2022). GISD30: global 30 m impervious-surface dynamic dataset from 1985 to 2020 using time-series Landsat imagery on the Google Earth Engine platform. Earth System Science Data 14, 1831–1856.

datasets.pff_known_issues: Confuses some bare rock and high-albedo natural surfaces with impervious — disabled by default to avoid false-positive disturbance buffers in mountainous / arid regions.

datasets.name: GISA — Global 30 m Impervious Surface Area 1972–2019
datasets.role_in_pff: Optional supplementary built-up source. Currently DISABLED by default (includeGISA=false) due to similar rock false-positive issues as GISD30.
datasets.description: First global ISA dataset extending to 1972 (longest time span), produced from >3M Landsat scenes with a locally adaptive classifier. Pixel value encodes years since 1972 of impervious onset; F-score 0.954 on 120,777 reference sites.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: gisa.mosaic().lte(year-1972) → binary; selfMask. Would OR into builtUpSmall if includeGISA were flipped on.

citation.text: Huang, X., Li, J., Yang, J., Zhang, Z., Li, D., Liu, X. (2021). 30 m global impervious surface area dynamics and urban expansion pattern observed by Landsat satellites: From 1972 to 2019. Science China Earth Sciences 64, 1922–1933.

datasets.pff_known_issues: See GISD30 — same rock-formation false-positive concern.

datasets.name: DLR WSF 2015
datasets.role_in_pff: Not used. Referenced in a commented-out line in timeSeriesAnthro.js as an alternative settlement layer.
datasets.description: 10 m global settlement mask for 2015 (Built-up = 255). Anchor for WSF Evolution.

citation.text: Marconcini, M. et al. (2020). Outlining where humans live, the World Settlement Footprint 2015. Scientific Data 7, 242.

datasets.name: DLR WSF 2019 (sat-io)
datasets.role_in_pff: Not used. Commented-out alternative in timeSeriesAnthro.js.
datasets.description: Updated 10 m WSF mask anchored to 2019.

citation.text: Marconcini, M. et al. (2021). Understanding Current Trends in Global Urbanisation – The World Settlement Footprint suite. GI_Forum 1, 33–38.

datasets.name: ORNL LandScan Global (sat-io mirror)
datasets.role_in_pff: Helper module loads LandScan via processLandscanPop / getLandscanForYear, exported from timeSeriesAnthro.js. NOT consumed by the pff_4 analysis chain in v4.14.1 (no caller in pff_4.js). Kept exposed so the workshop / scripts can use it (e.g. for population-weighted distance buffers).
datasets.description: 30 arc-second (~1 km) global ambient-population grid produced annually by ORNL using a smart-disaggregation approach combining census, remote sensing and machine learning. 'Ambient' = average over 24 hours.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Filter to target year; for years < 2000 reuse the 2000 image with year metadata overwritten.

citation.text: Rose, A.N., McKee, J.J., Sims, K.M., Bright, E.A., Reith, A.E., Urban, M.L. (2025). LandScan Global 30 Arcsecond Annual Global Gridded Population Datasets from 2000 to 2022. Scientific Data 12, 458.

datasets.name: GLC_FCS30D — Global 30 m Land-Cover Dynamics 1985–2022
datasets.role_in_pff: Source for the agriculture / cropland landcover backbone via timeseriesAnthroModule.preprocessGlc(). Combined with GLAD croplands (Potapov), Global Pasture Watch, Descals oil palm, and SDPT class 2 to produce the agriculture exclusion layer.
datasets.description: First global 30 m fine-classification (35 classes) land-cover dynamics dataset, generated with continuous change detection over the dense Landsat archive on GEE. PFF maps the GLC-FCS classes to a binary agriculture mask.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Combines five-year-map (≤2000) and annual (>2000) collections, picks the closest target-year image (1990, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020), mosaics; downstream the cropland classes are extracted.

citation.text: Zhang, X., Zhao, T., Xu, H., Liu, W., Wang, J., Chen, X., Liu, L. (2024). GLC_FCS30D: the first global 30 m land-cover dynamics monitoring product with a fine classification system for the period from 1985 to 2022 generated using dense-time-series Landsat imagery and the continuous change-detection method. Earth System Science Data 16, 1353–1381.

datasets.name: GLAD Global Cropland 2000–2019 (Potapov)
datasets.role_in_pff: Cropland source for the agriculture-disturbance buffer. Forward-filled in time so once cropland appears it stays present in later years (cumulative OR), preventing cropland from 'reverting' to forest.
datasets.temporal_coverage: 4-year epochs 2000–2003, 2004–2007, 2008–2011, 2012–2015, 2016–2019. PFF maps these to representative years 2000, _, 2010, 2015, 2020. For 1990 the 2003 asset is used as a proxy (acknowledged limitation).
datasets.description: Globally consistent cropland extent at 30 m. Cropland = land used for annual or perennial herbaceous crops (food, forage, biofuel). Excludes perennial woody crops, permanent pasture, shifting cultivation.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Each per-year asset mosaicked + tagged with year + Jan-1 system:time_start. Forward-fill OR keeps cropland cumulative across the time series.

citation.text: Potapov, P., Turubanova, S., Hansen, M.C., Tyukavina, A., Zalles, V., Khan, A., Song, X.-P., Pickens, A., Shen, Q., Cortez, J. (2022). Global maps of cropland extent and change show accelerated cropland expansion in the twenty-first century. Nature Food 3, 19–28.

datasets.name: Global Pasture Watch — Annual Dominant Class of Grasslands v1
datasets.role_in_pff: Pasture / grassland source for the agriculture-disturbance buffer. Cultivated-grassland pixels (class 1) are extracted, forward-filled, and OR'd into the agriculture composite alongside cropland and tree-crops.
datasets.description: Annual 30 m global maps of grassland class (cultivated vs natural/semi-natural) and extent, produced by per-class spatiotemporal random-forest models trained on 2.3M visually-interpreted samples plus GLAD ARD-2 Landsat, climate, landform and proximity covariates. PFF treats class 1 (cultivated grassland — actively managed pasture / forage) as agriculture; class 2 (natural / semi-natural) is NOT excluded.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: .eq(1) per image, year tagged from system:index, then forwardFillBinaryTimeSeries() so once cultivated-grass appears, it stays.

citation.text: Parente, L., Sloat, L., Mesquita, V., Consoli, D., Stanimirova, R., Hengl, T., Bonannella, C., Teixeira Cavalcante, R., Schultz, J., Frantz, D. et al. (2024). Annual 30-m maps of global grassland class and extent (2000–2022) based on spatiotemporal Machine Learning. Scientific Data 11, 1303.

datasets.name: Descals Global Oil Palm Year-of-Planting (YoP) 1990–2021
datasets.role_in_pff: Per-year oil-palm extent built from the year-of-planting raster: pixels with YoP ≤ analysisYear count as oil palm. Classified as Other Land with Tree Cover (OLTC, FRA Note 10), NOT as planted forest, so it routes into the agriculture/disturbance bucket and into the 02b_other_land_with_tree_cover export.
datasets.temporal_coverage: Year-of-planting 1990–2021 (Sentinel-1 extent at 10 m; Landsat-derived YoP at 30 m)
datasets.description: Global 30 m raster of the year an oil-palm plantation pixel was established (1990–2021). Industrial + smallholder palm extent from a CNN on Sentinel-1 (2016–2021) is back-cast through the Landsat archive to estimate planting year. PFF transforms the YoP image (decimal-year via minNBR_date / 365 + 1970, capped to 1989) into a per-year cumulative mask.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: _oilPalmYoP = mosaic(minNBR_date) / 365 + 1970, .min(1989); per-year mask = _oilPalmYoP.lte(year).

citation.text: Descals, A., Gaveau, D.L.A., Wich, S., Szantoi, Z., Meijaard, E. (2024). Global mapping of oil palm planting year from 1990 to 2021. Earth System Science Data 16, 5111–5129.

datasets.name: Spatial Database of Planted Trees (SDPT) v2
datasets.role_in_pff: Two-class split: class 1 (Planted Forests — timber/pulp/fibre) is the FRA-aligned Planted Forest layer (02d_planted_forest); class 2 (Tree Crops — fruit, agroforestry, RUBBER) is treated per FRA Note 10 as agriculture (Other Land with Tree Cover, 02b) and routed into the disturbance composite.
datasets.temporal_coverage: 2020 baseline (158 countries, ~264 Mha planted forest + 65 Mha tree crops)
datasets.description: Global compilation differentiating planted forests + tree crops from natural forests, integrating government and research data across 158 countries. Class 1 = Planted Forest (eucalyptus, pine, teak, etc.); class 2 = Tree Crops (rubber, oil palm, coconut, fruit orchards).
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: .unmask(0); class 1 .eq(1) → planted_forest layer; class 2 .eq(2) → tree-crops layer. CAVEAT: rubber lives in class 2 even though FRA Note 7 lists rubberwood as forest — workshop/Custom-exclusion override required if you want rubber rerouted.

citation.text: Richter, J., Goldman, E., Harris, N., Gibbs, D., Rose, M., Peyer, S., Richardson, S., Velappan, H. (2024). Spatial Database of Planted Trees (SDPT Version 2.0). Technical Note. World Resources Institute, Washington, DC.

datasets.name: FDAP Palm Probability — model 2024a
datasets.role_in_pff: Loaded but DISABLED in the production pipeline (the .or(fdapCommoditiesLargePatches) line in processingPlantationsMosaic is commented out). Reason: FDAP probability layers commit primary forest as palm — see auto-memory note 'FDAP commission errors in primary forest'.
datasets.description: 10 m per-pixel probability of oil-palm presence from a community-trained ML model. Default high-confidence threshold in the helper = 0.95.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Filter date 2020-01-01–2020-12-31; .first().gt(0.95). Goes through a smoothRadius=30 m boxcar twice with thresholds 0.4 and 0.4 for noise removal — but the resulting layer is NOT currently OR'd into the plantations mosaic.

citation.text: Forest Data Partnership / Google (2024). FDAP Palm Probability model 2024a.

datasets.license: CC-BY-NC 4.0 for non-commercial; commercial terms separate
datasets.pff_known_issues: Commits primary forest as palm in some humid-tropical regions. Stay disabled in PFF pending model improvement (see /memory/feedback_qgis* for context).

datasets.name: FDAP Rubber Probability — model 2024a
datasets.role_in_pff: Loaded but DISABLED for the same reason as FDAP Palm.
datasets.description: 10 m per-pixel probability of rubber-plantation presence. Default high-confidence threshold = 0.95.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Filter 2020; .first().gt(0.95). NOT currently OR'd into plantations mosaic.

citation.text: Forest Data Partnership / Google (2024). FDAP Rubber Probability model 2024a.

datasets.pff_known_issues: Commission errors in primary forest. Disabled by default.

datasets.name: FDAP Cocoa Probability — model 2024a
datasets.role_in_pff: Loaded but DISABLED for the same reason as FDAP Palm.
datasets.description: 10 m per-pixel probability of cocoa-plantation presence. Default high-confidence threshold = 0.90.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Filter 2020; .first().gt(0.90). NOT currently OR'd into plantations mosaic.

citation.text: Forest Data Partnership / Google (2024). FDAP Cocoa Probability model 2024a.

datasets.pff_known_issues: Commission errors in primary forest. Disabled by default.

datasets.name: GRIP4 — Global Roads Inventory Project (with predicted AADT)
datasets.role_in_pff: Per-year 'roads with traffic' raster. Linearly interpolated between 1990, 2000, 2015 anchor years; 2020 = copy of 2015 (latest available). Used (alongside the OSM roads raster) for the road-buffer disturbance distance.

derived_assets.preprocessing: GRIP4 vector with a predicted AADT (Annual Average Daily Traffic) attribute, rasterised via reduceToImage(['median'], Reducer.max()). 1990 / 2000 / 2015 versions uploaded; intermediate years linearly interpolated.

datasets.description: Harmonised vector of ~60 source road datasets at global scale. PFF uses a derivative with predicted AADT (Annual Average Daily Traffic) rasterised per anchor year.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Lazy-cached per-year FeatureCollection → reduceToImage. Bilinear-style year interpolation between anchors (year ≤ 1990 → 1990; year > 2015 → 2015).

citation.text: Meijer, J.R., Huijbregts, M.A.J., Schotten, C.G.J., Schipper, A.M. (2018). Global patterns of current and future road infrastructure. Environmental Research Letters 13, 064006.

datasets.pff_known_issues: AADT prediction layer is a derived (custom) product — re-citation should include 'derived AADT prediction, 2024-03-12 snapshot, andyarnellgee'.

datasets.name: OSM Roads (PFF custom 33-region merge)
datasets.role_in_pff: Static (untimestamped) global OSM roads, used as the 'small roads' raster for the disturbance-buffer distance. Vector form (33 chunked FeatureCollections) is exported per-AOI for the QGIS plugin's roads input slot.
datasets.description: Custom merge of all OpenStreetMap 'highway=*' linestrings from Geofabrik regional PBFs. Processed locally with pyosmium → GeoPackage → CSV chunks (≤10 GB each) → GEE FeatureCollections (33 children). Rasterised to a single global 30 m presence image aligned to the Hansen GFC grid. Caveats: no road-class differentiation (some highways are foot/bike-only), 'proposed' / 'planned' values dropped during ingestion.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: Vector path (export only): per-asset filterBounds(aoi) + ee.Filter.intersects() two-stage clip; flatten; drop highway ∈ {'proposed','planned'}. Raster path (analysis): pre-built mosaic via roadsMosaicStatic().
datasets.provenance_doc: docs/osm_roads_prep (text file with full asset list + collection dates + processing chain)

citation.text: OpenStreetMap contributors (2025). Planet dump retrieved via Geofabrik regional PBFs ~21 May 2025 (Europe ~29 May 2025).

datasets.name: JRC Tropical Moist Forest — Deforestation Year (v1 2025 release)
datasets.role_in_pff: Tropical-belt deforestation-year raster combined with Hansen lossyear (and treecover2000>10%) into the disturbance composite used by forest_disturbances() — drives parts of the 'forest lost before analysisYear' subtraction.
datasets.description: Annual tropical-moist-forest cover-change product produced by JRC from the full Landsat archive. The DeforestationYear band gives the year of detected deforestation (≥1990 = deforested in or before that year).
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: filter year ≤ analysisYear; mosaic; .gte(1990) → binary disturbed mask. OR'd with Hansen lossyear-derived loss to get total disturbance pre-analysisYear.

citation.text: Vancutsem, C., Achard, F., Pekel, J.-F., Vieilledent, G., Carboni, S., Simonetti, D., Gallego, J., Aragão, L.E.O.C., Nasi, R. (2021). Long-term (1990–2019) monitoring of forest cover changes in the humid tropics. Science Advances 7, eabe1603.

datasets.name: OSM Water Layer (sat-io / U-Tokyo)
datasets.role_in_pff: Loaded for canal extraction (band==4 = canal). Currently NOT in the default disturbance composite — code computes osmCanals but the result is only commented-out shown on map. Available for navigable-river / canal disturbance buffers if wired up.
datasets.description: Global rasterised OSM surface-water layer (3 arc-sec; rivers / lakes / reservoirs / canals) extracted from the OSM planet PBF using natural=water, waterway=*, landuse=reservoir tags. Maintained by Yamazaki Lab.
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: median().eq(4) for canals.

citation.text: Yamazaki Lab, U-Tokyo. OSM Water Layer derived from OpenStreetMap.

datasets.name: PFF Navigable Rivers (custom from WDB / global river database)
datasets.role_in_pff: Loaded for navigable-river extraction; rasterised. Currently held in the script but not actively buffered into the default disturbance composite (only paint() and updateMask happen).
datasets.description: Custom-prepared PFF asset deriving from a World Database / global navigable-rivers source. See preprocessing/wdb/ for provenance (if present).
datasets.preprocessing_in_pff: ee.Image().paint(fc, 1).updateMask(country_and_buffer_mask).

citation.text: Custom PFF derivative — original World Database (WDB) navigable rivers source. Cite original WDB / NGA where applicable.

datasets.name: PFF Navigable Waterways USA (custom)

datasets.description: Custom-prepared FeatureCollection of USA navigable waterways.

datasets.name: WRI SBTN Natural Lands Map v1.1 (2020)

datasets.description: Pan-European database of primary and old-growth forest polygons compiled from country-level submissions and remote-sensing verification (Sabatini et al. 2018, 2021).

datasets.name: WUR Congo Basin Logging Roads
datasets.role_in_pff: Not used in default. Helper getCongoRoadsUpToYear() exists in timeSeriesAnthro.js with a year-based accumulation chain (Kleinschroth pre-2003, 2003–2018, monthly 2019–2020, post-2020) — workshop swap-in for Congo Basin national runs.

code_refs.function: getCongoRoadsUpToYear (defined but not called from pff_4.js)

datasets.description: Wageningen University & Research distribution of logging-road detections for the Congo Basin, with monthly resolution 2019-01 → 2024-12. Combined with Kleinschroth et al. (2019) historical road classes (old / new) for pre-2019 coverage.

citation.text: Kleinschroth, F., Laporte, N., Laurance, W.F., Goetz, S.J., Ghazoul, J. (2019). Road expansion and persistence in forests of the Congo Basin. Nature Sustainability 2, 628–634.
